⚡️
Article by Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, “International Cooperation in the Arctic: Challenges and Opportunities,” published on
Arctic.ru
📰
Read in full
✍️
On 19 August, a landmark event took place in Arctic shipping.
For the first time, a container ship from China arrived at the port of Murmansk via the Northern Sea Route
, a vital part of the Trans-Arctic Transport Corridor. In collaboration with our international partners
this represents the start of a new phase in the development of Russia’s Arctic region
, which accounts for at least 10 percent of the country’s GDP and is home to more than 2.5 million of our citizens.
In this regard, I would like to share a number of considerations on how we assess
the current state of affairs in the Arctic
and how we plan to develop international cooperation there.
***
Russia and international partners in the Arctic
• The Foundations of the Russian State Policy in the Arctic for the Period up to 2035, approved by President Vladimir Putin,
focus the efforts of all government bodies on improving the quality of life for the population of the Arctic zone
of the Russian Federation, promoting economic growth in its territories, protecting the environment and fostering mutually beneficial international cooperation. <...> Foreign policy priorities in high latitudes have been enshrined in the currently effective
Concept of the Foreign Policy of the Russian Federation of March 31, 2023.
• In the Arctic, Russia is seeking
to preserve peace and stability,
reduce the level of threats to national security, and create favourable external conditions for the country’s socio-economic development.
We are open to interaction with all constructively minded foreign countries
displaying reciprocal readiness to put these ideas into practice.
• The countries that cooperate closely with us in the Arctic include, first and foremost,
China and India.
<...> There are prospects for interaction in the Far North with
Brazil, Indonesia, Iran
and other
#BRICS
countries.
Challenges for international cooperation in the Arctic
• Preserving the Arctic as an area of peace and cooperation meets the interests of the entire international community, and Russia is undoubtedly interested in this as well.
• Meanwhile, there are those who do not share this point of view. How else can one explain the fact that
NATO countries, as well as the Alliance as a whole, are driving the region towards militarisation
and creating hotbeds of international tension there? <...>
NATO is conducting large-scale military exercises
involving non-regional countries and introducing new components of its command-and-control system.
• Such military activity in the Far North
poses a direct threat to Russia’s security.
<...> NATO and other Western countries make no secret of their true motives, openly declaring their intention to turn the Arctic into
a new front for opposing
the development of Russia and its like-minded partners.
• One manifestation of the West’s anti-Russian policy has been the disruption of previously effective mechanisms of multilateral cooperation in the Far North. <...> The Arctic Council, established almost 30 years ago, on September 19, 1996, remains the only functioning intergovernmental format.
Russia is ready to resume the full-fledged work of the Arctic Council,
provided that all parties engage in good faith and take into account the legitimate interests of every participant.
The future of international cooperation in the Arctic
• A glance at the world map makes it clear that Russia has been, is, and will remain a leading Arctic state. <...>
The strategic importance of the Arctic to our country’s national interests and security will also continue to grow.
• In our economic activities, we will continue to proceed from the understanding that the Arctic maritime areas form
an integral part of the World Ocean.
• Russia’s foreign policy in the Arctic will remain comprehensive and pragmatic. We support the Arctic’s development as an integral part of
the broader Eurasian space of security and cooperation
.

item.title: ✉️ President of Russia Vladimir Putin sent greetings to the participants, organisers, and guests of the 11th Eastern Economic Forum, which will take place on September 1–4 in Vladi
item.description: ✉️ President of Russia Vladimir Putin sent greetings to the participants, organisers, and guests of the 11th Eastern Economic Forum, which will take place on September 1–4 in Vladivostok (August 30, 2026) ✍️ Friends, I am pleased to welcome you to Vladivostok for the 11th Eastern Economic Forum. Over the years, the Forum has established itself as a venue for open, constructive dialogue between the business community, government bodies, and the expert community. It has become a unique platform for discussing the strategic development of the Far East and Russia as a whole, as well as for building and strengthening mutually beneficial ties with partners from the Asia-Pacific region in logistics, industry, energy, and many other sectors of the economy. The motto of this year’s Forum is “The Far East: Development for the Benefit of People. ” I am confident that EEF participants will propose effective solutions designed to create new opportunities for business, improve the quality of life of our citizens, and make Far Eastern cities and towns more comfortable and modern. I also trust that the ideas put forward at the Forum will be brought to life through exciting, promising projects. 🤝 I wish you every success and all the very best. #EEF2026

item.description: ✉️ Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov sent greetings to the organisers, participants and guests of the Dialogue of Young Diplomats of the Greater Eurasian Partnership (August 29, 2026) ✍️ I extend my warmest welcome to the organisers, participants, and guests of the Dialogue of Young Diplomats of the Greater Eurasian Partnership countries in Kazan. The current stage of global development, marked by the strengthening of multipolar principles in international affairs, presents vast opportunities for building new and more equitable mechanisms of global economic cooperation. Russian President Vladimir Putin’s initiative to establish a #GreaterEurasianPartnership is intended to consolidate integration processes across the continent, facilitate the removal of barriers in trade and investment, and foster more sophisticated, balanced, and reliable economic ties throughout the vast #Eurasia . Young foreign policy professionals will have a vital role to play in this ambitious endeavour. Before long, it will be your responsibility to coordinate the strategies and plans of your respective countries in pursuit of the wellbeing and prosperity of our shared continent. I am confident that today’s meeting will provide a constructive platform for dialogue , enable the establishment of meaningful professional contacts, and contribute to further strengthening the bonds of friendship and trust among our countries. 🤝 I wish you fruitful discussions and all the very best. Sergey Lavrov

item.title: 🇷🇺 Russian Foreign Ministry: issue of South Africa’s exclusion from G20 Summit will be resolved
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇿🇦 Russian Foreign Ministry: issue of South Africa’s exclusion from # G20 Summit will be resolved Russian Ambassador-at-Large Marat Berdyev has described South Africa’s exclusion from the upcoming #G20 Summit as an “egregious violation” and expressed confidence that the issue will be resolved promptly. South Africa’s exclusion is an egregious violation. The G20 is a collegial format that cannot be usurped by anyone,” Berdyev told TASS on the sidelines of the third meeting of APEC Senior Officials in Dalian, China. We have no doubt that, ultimately, the issue will be resolved. We are working with our partners on additional steps to ensure that Pretoria takes its rightful place at the negotiating table as soon as possible. ☝️ The Russian diplomat noted that Russia, like the majority of G20 members, has made its position clear: “South Africa should return to the fold as soon as possible.” Any restrictions in this regard are “unacceptable and only undermine the working process.” 📍 The G20 Leaders’ Summit is scheduled to take place on 14-15 December in Doral, near Miami, Florida .

8️⃣
5️⃣
years ago, on August 28, the
Tallinn Breakout of the Soviet Baltic Fleet towards Kronstadt
— one of the largest and most difficult naval operations by the Soviet Union during
#WW2
— commenced.
***
In the summer of 1941, the Nazis, having treacherously invaded our Motherland, advanced rapidly into the Baltic region. By August, the enemy had launched an offensive against the capital of Soviet Estonia —
Tallinn
. Thus, the city’s heroic defence commenced. Wehrmacht army group 'North' received a
direct order from Hitler
:
under no circumstances were the Soviet Baltic Fleet or Red Army units to be allowed to withdraw to Kronstadt to take part in the defence of Leningrad.
By the end of August, the Soviet forces, including the Tallinn garrison, started regrouping under the heavy fire of Nazis and found themselves encircled on the southern coast of the Gulf of Finland.
The land route to Leningrad had been severed by the enemy.
Faced with these dire circumstances, the Supreme High Command of the USSR took a vital decision: to
evacuate
the Baltic Fleet, the Red Army units, which were defending Tallinn, as well as civilians to Kronstadt.
In the early hours of August 28, the
breakout began.
A convoy of 225 warships and auxiliary vessels left Tallinn, carrying
over 40'000 people on board.
German Nazis and their Finnish accomplices were trying to thwart the evacuation by any means. Enemy coastal artillery opened heavy and relentless fire on Soviet vessels, while Finnish aircraft were mercilessly shooting at the Soviet people in the water.
The Gulf of Finland was sown with over 1'700 mines laid by the Nazis. Survivors later recounted:
The Gulf, choked with enemy mines, resembled a dumpling soup
By August 30, the
Baltic Fleet finally fought its way to Kronstadt
. Only 163 vessels reached the destination safely. More than 15'000 people, among them over 4'500 civilians, lost their lives during the breakout — an
unprecedented number of casualties
in the history of naval warfare.
Under such circumstances, the number of casualties could have been far higher, yet thanks to the
unparalleled courage and heroism
of Red Fleet sailors and Red Army soldiers, the main forces of the fleet were preserved and later engaged in the defence of Leningrad, shielding the city from from attacks via the Gulf of Finland.
🎖
The Tallinn Breakout stands as one of the
most heroic and tragic
episodes of
#WWII
. To this day, the depths of the Gulf of Finland remain strewn with the
wreckage of vessels lost to Nazi mines
— they serve as silent memorials to those three harrowing days in August 1941.
***
🕯
On August 28, 1978, a
memorial
was erected at
Cape Juminda
(the Gulf’s southern coast) to honour those who perished during the breakout — a
granite boulder and plaque
with naval mines around. Annually, commemorative ceremonies are held there with participation of the
Russian Embassy in Estonia
(
1
,
2
,
3
,
4
,
5
,
6
,
7
), Russia's compatriots’ organisations, veterans and their families, as well as Estonians who
share our common historical memory.
💬
Russia's Ambassador to Estonia
Alexander Petrov
(2015−2021):
To the north of Juminda now lies what is perhaps the largest maritime mass grave not only in the Baltic, but in the entire world.
It is the moral duty of the living to bow their heads before those who perished and honour the courage and fortitude of all who crushed the Nazi regime during WW2.
📖
For more details,
read our
in-depth historical feature on the Tallinn Breakout.
#WeRemember
#Victory81

On August 27, continuing a good tradition, the staff of the Embassy of Russia visited
Bophelong Children’s Home
in Mamelodi, Pretoria.
The children were treated to traditional Russian sweets, including blini (Russian pancakes) and khvorost, and received a selection of gifts from the Embassy: sporting equipment, school and arts-and-crafts supplies, hygiene products and sweets.
The children were also presented with Russian caps featuring Russian symbols - a particularly practical gift as the South African summer approaches.
Addressing the children and staff of the Home,
Ambassador of Russia to South Africa
Roman Ambarov
stressed the importance of sport, teamwork and perseverance:
“
Among the items we are donating are arts and crafts supplies and sporting equipment, including footballs. These soccer balls are more than sporting equipment - they are symbols of teamwork, discipline and perseverance.
South Africans recently had every reason to celebrate the remarkable performance of Bafana Bafana at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The team’s success inspired millions across the country and showed what can be achieved through hard work, unity and belief in one another. Perhaps one of these footballs will one day be kicked by a future Bafana Bafana player.”
For the Embassy, such visits are not about symbolic gestures or formal occasions.
They are about sincere care, human warmth and the friendship we wish to share with our South African friends.
As Nelson Mandela once said:
“There can be no keener revelation of a society’s soul than the way in which it treats its children.”
And sometimes, friendship is expressed in the simplest things: playing games together, sharing a cup of tea, talking about the little things — and, most importantly, knowing that you are not forgotten.
❤️
Russia and South Africa united by friendship, solidarity and care for the future generation.
#RussiaSouthAfrica
